name: Walkability Through Different Lenses (Michigan street pairs)
description: Method replication: same task, aspects and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of the same towns, © Google). Wedyan, Yeh, Saeidi-Rizi, Peng & Chang (2025, PLOS ONE 20:e0322078) compared how people and GPT-4o judge walkability. 174 online participants saw pairs of street photos from Lansing, East Lansing and Williamston, Michigan; each pair belonged to one of six aspects: overall walkability (ease and appeal of walking), feasibility (practicality of walking), accessibility (for people of diverse abilities), safety, comfort and liveliness. For each pair they rated both photos from 1 to 10 and explained in at least 20 words why the higher-rated photo was better; GPT-4o got the same pairs and prompt 15 times each. People and GPT-4o picked the same photo for overall walkability, feasibility, accessibility and safety but differed on comfort and liveliness; people's reasons covered more topics and stressed natural features and atmosphere, GPT-4o's stressed infrastructure and practical use. Analysis as in the paper: per pair, which photo won (equal ratings dropped), agreement with a model run on the same pairs, then text analysis of the explanations (sentiment, LDA topics, keyword frequencies, similarity between human and model reasons). Differences from the original study: (1) the paper used 96 iPhone photos taken from the sidewalk, paired once into 48 fixed pairs split over 8 survey groups; this template bundles 59 Google Street View views (2016–2026) from the three towns and draws a new random pair for every aspect, so each participant sees 6 pairs; (2) the six aspect definitions are shown on the intro screen and on each pair; the paper's pilot-tested wording is not published, so these follow the paper's one-line definitions; (3) the 20-word minimum is enforced by the page; (4) the background questions follow the paper's reported demographics (gender, age, urban or rural residence, country, walking frequency and weekly walking time), with our wording.
author: Wedyan, Yeh, Saeidi-Rizi, Peng & Chang
